title: Existence of a nondeterministic effective code scheme
statement: There exists an effective coding scheme for nondeterministic two-work-tape Turing machines over the binary alphabet: it has an encoding and a total decoder such that, for every coded machine $M$ and every natural number $m$, decoding the encoding of $M$ followed by $m$ copies of the bit $1$ returns $M$. The scheme also includes a finite binary-alphabet Turing machine and a time bound that, on every binary input string, compute the fixed serialization of the machine decoded from that string.
replaced:
There exists a coding scheme for nondeterministic two-work-tape machines over the binary
alphabet, with a total decoder, such that encoding a machine and appending any finite
number of true bits decodes to that same machine. The scheme also has a finite binary
Turing machine and a time bound that compute, on every binary string, the fixed
serialization of the machine decoded from that string.
